name: Ironlimb Bastionleg MK-IV Combat Series
product_name: Ironlimb Bastionleg MK-IV Combat Leg System
description:
The Bastionleg MK-IV is a military-lineage full leg replacement built from hardened titanium-alloy with reinforced knee and hip interface joints rated to 900kg compressive load. The system integrates a magnetic boot interface in the heel and toe plate compatible with ferrous surfaces and standard combat vehicle flooring, and a layered hydraulic-pneumatic impact absorption stack in the knee that converts fall energy into stored pressure for assisted jump launches. Onboard gyroscopic stabilizers maintain balance during high-G maneuvers and surface recoil events. The MK-IV added civilian licensing provisions to the MK-III military frame, primarily by removing the integrated weapon hardpoints.

The Bastionleg is the limb of choice for private security contractors, licensed bounty hunters, and former military personnel who couldn't part with hardware that kept them alive. In the lower tiers it's grey-market common — the military surplus pipeline leaks MK-IIIs constantly, and chop-shop techs hack the restricted firmware to civilian-adjacent compliance. Street culture treats the Bastionleg as a mark of serious professional violence, and most civilians give wearers visible deference.
installation_requirements: Licensed combat-prosthetics surgeon, bilateral installation strongly recommended for balance calibration, 6-week load-bearing rehabilitation
rejection_risk: Moderate — titanium alloy frame requires extended osseointegration; hydraulic fluid biocompatibility varies by patient
maintenance: Hydraulic fluid flush every 6 months; joint armor inspection after combat use; magnetic interface recalibration annually

cultural_context: The Bastionleg MK-IV carries the unmistakable visual grammar of institutional violence — thick plated shins, matte-black joint housings, and the distinctive magnetic heel click on hard floors. Security professionals wear them openly as deterrence signaling. In Tier 1-2 districts, encountering someone on Bastionlegs means calculating exit routes before saying hello.
